doc.title: Young Snooky — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The Lunceford trumpeter named Steve before Paul Webster
summary: Young identifies Steve as the high-note trumpeter who played Rhythm Is Our Business before Paul Webster joined.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Ok, ok, ok. I think you‘ve said enough. [Laughs] But, let‘s see, so… Gerald Wilson replaced Sy Oliver and you replaced Eddie Tompkins.
Before them, let me see, you had Paul Webster.
That‘s back when I‘m talking about.

Steve was the high note trumpet player. He‘s the one that played ―Rhythm is Our Business.‖ And that kind of helped make Jimmie Lunceford famous. Steve played ―Rhythm is Our Business.‖ [Sings] ―Rhythm is our business, rhythm is what we sell. Rhythm is our business, rhythm is what we sell. Steve he‘s the guy that hits ‗em makes you think he‘s in the sky.‖ [sings]
Ok, hang on, hang on, we‘re going to get Steve. Hang on, we‘re going to find out the Steve you‘re talking about. Damn.
